title: Compact halo attention kernel with rotary-slot merging, continuous prefetch and KV-evict hints
author: Elena Martinez
description:
Context: We observed regressions in throughput for medium-length sequences (128-512) under mixed workloads with large identical prefixes. Prior Flash-style kernels were good for long dense sequences but had tail inefficiencies when many requests shared partial prefixes and when small microbatches competed for GPU lanes. This PR introduces a compact 'halo' attention kernel that reduces memory traffic for the common prefix case and a lightweight rotary-slot merging layer to avoid redundant rotary rotations across coalesced KV windows.

Summary: Implement a new CUDA kernel (compact_halo_kernel.cu) that: 1) performs a tiled attention compute with halo regions to reuse overlap between consecutive windows; 2) fuses QKV transpose and scaling in a single pass optimized for fp16; 3) exposes a rotary-slot merging API so the runtime can collapse identical rotary state across requests in a continuous batch; 4) integrates KV cache eviction hints to prefer warm lanes and avoid global cache thrash. The scheduler changes add a continuous-batcher policy that groups requests by rotary-slot fingerprint and sequence-length bucket, enabling sustained high occupancy without raising p99.

Commits (high-level): - feat(attn): add compact halo attention CUDA microkernel and wrapper (Elena) - perf(attn): fuse qkv transpose + scale pass, use warp-level reductions (Elena) - feat(rotary): rotary slot manager and merge path exposed to runtime (Arjun) - perf(kv): eviction hint headers and warm-lane prioritizer (Priya) - infra: add integration test and benchmark harness + CI job (Liam)

Files/touchpoints: The main novel files are runtimes/attn/compact_halo_kernel.cu and runtimes/attn/rotary_slot_manager.cc. The continuous batcher (scheduler/continuous_batcher.rs) contains the grouping policy and new metrics emission hooks. tests/attn/test_compact_halo_integration.py exercises single-node Dedicated and hosted-mode fallbacks. docs/attn/compact_halo.md documents expected latency/cost tradeoffs and recommended config flags.

Benchmarks & results: Microbenchmarks run on p4d.24xlarge equivalent nodes with mixed traffic (short prefix share 60%, seq=256 median): - baseline (current main flash-like kernel): p50=12.8ms, p95=42.6ms, tokens/s=74k, cost/unit=1.00 - compact-halo kernel + rotary-merge: p50=9.1ms (-29%), p95=27.8ms (-35%), tokens/s=102k (+38%), cost/unit=0.73 (-27%) For long sequences (>1024) the kernel falls back to the existing fused-flash path; regression is <3% on p50. Memory usage: per-GPU kv-cache peak reduced by ~12% under high prefix locality due to shared rotary slots.

Testing: Added unit tests around rotary-slot fingerprint collisions and eviction hints. Integration harness runs end-to-end on dedicated staging nodes plus a smoke test against hosted API to validate graceful fallback. CI matrix includes CUDA 12.1, cuda 11.8 (legacy), and an emulated CPU path for fuzzing. All tests green on CI; a transient perf job required a second run on the p4 job which passed on rerun.

Review discussion (excerpted): - Samir Rao: "Nice kernel shape; please add comments describing the halo indexing math and why we choose 64x8 tiles." Elena: "Added detailed inline docs and a diagram in the .md; the tile sizes were tuned for SMx architecture across our benchmark fleet." - Liam O'Neill: "Concern: rotary-slot merge correctness under async cache eviction." Arjun: "Merged windows use a lightweight refcount and a compare-and-swap on the slot table; eviction code now checks refcount and falls back to a deep-copy path if racing." - Priya Gupta: "Please add metrics for slot-collisions and warm-lane hit-rate." Elena: "Added counters and a per-route tag exposed in the console. Will follow up with dashboards in a follow-up PR."

Compatibility & rollout: The runtime exposes a feature flag runtime.attn.compact_halo and a route-level override. Rollout plan: enable on canary fleet (10% traffic) for 72h with automatic rollback on latency regression >10% or error spike. A/B test against the fused-flash kernel for cost/quality checks.

Merge outcome: squashed and merged to main on 2024-11-21 (merge_commit: 8b3d6f4a6ef3c2d9b1c4f9a7c2ae5e01b3d4f9a0). Release notes: "Introduce compact halo attention kernel with rotary-slot merging and KV warm-lane hints; improves throughput for mixed-length workloads and reduces per-token cost when prefix locality is high."

Related work & follow-ups: This PR intentionally keeps the long-sequence fastpath in place; follow-ups include a cross-kernel autotuner to pick halo vs flash based on real-time telemetry and a tenant-aware slot compaction background job.

Notes: No breaking API changes; added small public runtime flag and internal metrics. Backported a minimal portion of the eviction hint header to the 2024.10 release branch in a separate hotfix PR for an ongoing customer experiment.
